stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:

  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

## Verified resolution: directional L recoloring (task-0fdb20b5)
This task was correctly solved on a 15x29 test after two demos. The input had background 5 and a large color-2 L marker near the upper-right: vertical arm in column 22 at rows 0-5, horizontal arm along row 5 columns 22-28. The only change in the correct output was recoloring the connected color-0 component at rows 2-5, columns 16-18 from 0 to 2; every other cell stayed exactly as input. Rule from demos: keep grid dimensions and walls, recolor with 4 only the background-color cells enclosed by the line color. The line itself is not recolored. Color values vary; fill is consistently 4.

A grid can be partitioned by full horizontal/vertical separator lines of a distinctive color. Ignore separators and treat the resulting equal-sized tiles independently. Practical approach: identify full-line separators and crop tiles; use demos to establish the encoding exactly, since rule mapping differed across the two examples above. ## Continual-ARC verified rule: mirrored triple tiling (task-3fb47f44; 2026-09-29)
The input is an arbitrary H×W grid. Output is 3H×2W. Horizontally, each row becomes its left-right reversal followed by the original row. Vertically, stack three H-row bands in order: input rows reversed, input rows forward, input rows reversed. Thus output[r] = concat(reverse(input[row]), input[row]), where row is selected by the band sequence `[H-1,...,0, 0,...,H-1, H-1,...,0]`. The repeated boundary rows are intentional.

Verified demo: 3×13 input became 9×26 with vertical source-row order `2,1,0,0,1,2,2,1,0`; every output row consists of the corresponding source row reversed then unchanged.
